sentences.text: 3. One Mohammed Khaseem met with an accident on 26.09.2008 and died subsequently.
His wife and children have filed a claim petition claiming compensation of Rs.16,50,000/-.

The Tribunal after considering the entire evidence on record, NC: 2026:KHC:6657 HC-KAR has awarded the compensation of Rs.4,50,000/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from 30.04.2012 (from the date of evidence) till the date of realization.
4. Aggrieved by the said judgment and award of the Tribunal, the wife and children have preferred this appeal contending that income of the Mohammed Khaseem was considered as Rs.3,000/- per month.
In fact he was earning Rs.450/- per day and there is evidence on record to show that the family was paying Rs.3,500/- per month towards rent and residential premises.
Further, no compensation was awarded under the head medical expenses, despite the fact that he was treated in the hospital immediately after the accident.
Hence, he prays for enhancement of compensation of the Tribunal.
5. It is stated that the Mohammed Khaseem was running a butcher shop and earning Rs.450/- per day.
But he has not filed any proof of income.
The accident had occurred in the year 2008.

As such,
the notional income is to be taken as Rs.4,500/- per month, as per the guidelines given by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
Mohammed Khaseem was aged 40 years at the time of the accident.

Therefore, 25% is to be NC: 2026:KHC:6657 HC-KAR added towards his future Nuzhada Khatoon vs Ibrahim on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55623524/

As per the guidelines of Hon'ble Apex Court in case of Sarla Verma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation, 1/4th of income of the deceased has to be deducted towards his personal expenses as there are 6 dependents.

sentences.text: As the deceased was aged 40 years, the multiplier of '15' is to be taken.

Therefore, 'loss of dependency' would come to Rs.7,59,375/- (5625 x 12 x 15 x ).
7.
This Court finds it just and reasonable to award Rs.40,000/- towards 'spousal consortium' for claimant No.1, Rs.40,000/- each towards 'parental consortium' for claimant Nos.2 to 6.

The claimants are also entitled for Rs.30,000/- towards conventional heads.
8.

Thus in all, the claimants are entitled for the following compensation:-

9.
The Tribunal has awarded the compensation of Rs.4,50,000/- but the claimants are entitled to total compensation of Rs.10,29,375/-.

Therefore, the claimants are entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.5,79,375/-
(Rs.10,29,375- Rs.4,50,000).
10.

ORDER i.
The appeal is allowed-in-part.

ii.
